title: LLM-Inference-Bench: Inference Benchmarking of Large Language Models on AI Accelerators
problem: LLMs require efficient hardware acceleration due to high computational demands, and their inference performance varies significantly across different hardware platforms and inference frameworks, making it difficult to identify optimal configurations.
motivation: Systematically benchmarking LLM inference performance across diverse hardware platforms is crucial for understanding scalability and throughput characteristics.
method: LLM-Inference-Bench tests how fast large language models (specifically LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen models at 7 billion and 70 billion parameters) run on different specialized hardware accelerators—Nvidia GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel Habana, and SambaNova chips—using various inference frameworks (the software that controls how the model executes). It measures the speed and resource efficiency of each hardware-software combination. An interactive dashboard lets you quickly see and compare results to find which configuration works best for your needs.
key_novelty: A benchmarking system that measures and compares LLM inference performance across different hardware accelerators and software frameworks, presenting results in an interactive dashboard.
contributions: Comprehensive benchmarking suite for LLM inference performance evaluation
Systematic analysis across diverse hardware platforms including GPUs and specialized AI accelerators
Evaluation of multiple LLM models and inference frameworks with detailed performance comparison
Interactive dashboard for identifying optimal configurations per hardware platform
limitations: Paper limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: LLM inference benchmarking across diverse AI accelerators
